title: The check
goals: The program ends with no error.
starting_code:
# This is the program that checks every broom, but it stops at the first one!
brooms = wizard.find_all("broom")
for broom in brooms:
    right = broom.position.x - wizard.position.x
    up = wizard.position.y - broom.position.y
    wizard.move_right(right)
    wizard.move_up(up)
    broom.untie()
hints: The program tries to untie every broom, but untying a broom with no knot is an error!
We only want to untie a broom if it actually has a knot. Look at its attribute to see if it is knotted before using the method.
Put an `if` inside the loop to look at `knotted`, just before untying, and don't forget to add spaces before the method so it's inside the `if`!
intro: {mate} has laid every single broom on the floor, from the corner to the hay, for a last look. A few escaped us and are still knotted! I took the last program and changed it to move right and up to check them all. But it stops at the first broom, because that one doesn't have a knot, and untying a broom with no knot is an error! The last broom is at (13, 6).
outro: Phew! Every broom is safe now. And just in time, I can hear the class coming!
learned: Now you know that an `if` inside a `for` decides in each turn, and that a method that needs something is used after looking at the attribute that says it.
